title: 8-Week Intermediate Muscle Gain & Fat Loss Plan (Back-Friendly)

context.injuries: I am dealing with some lower back and upper back issue. So have to avoid back heavy excercises like Deadlifts and excercises that strain upper back muscles like overhead press.

plan.title: 8-Week Intermediate Muscle Gain & Fat Loss Plan (Back-Friendly)

exercises.name: Incline Dumbbell Press
exercises.notes: Start with dumbbells you can control for 10-12 reps with good form (e.g., 20-30 lb per hand for male intermediate, 10-20 lb for female intermediate). Ensure shoulder blades are retracted and chest is leading the movement. Avoid arching your lower back excessively.

exercises.name: Flat Dumbbell Press
exercises.notes: Similar to incline, focus on controlling the weight down and pressing up. (e.g., 25-35 lb per hand for male, 12-22 lb for female). Keep feet flat on the floor for stability.

exercises.name: Cable Crossover (Low-to-Mid)
exercises.notes: Focus on a strong contraction in the inner and lower chest. Use a weight that allows full range of motion without straining. (e.g., 15-25 lb per side for male, 7.5-15 lb for female).

exercises.name: Dumbbell Lateral Raises
exercises.notes: Keep a slight bend in the elbows and lift the dumbbells to shoulder height, leading with the elbows. Avoid shrugging. (e.g., 10-15 lb for male, 5-10 lb for female).

exercises.name: Triceps Pushdown (Rope Attachment)
exercises.notes: Maintain elbows close to the body and extend fully, squeezing the triceps. (e.g., 40-60 lb for male, 20-35 lb for female).

exercises.name: Machine Dips (Assisted if needed)
exercises.notes: Adjust assistance as needed to perform 8-12 reps. Focus on a controlled descent and powerful push-up. If no machine, do Close-Grip Push-ups.

exercises.name: Leg Press
exercises.notes: Position feet hip-width apart, ensuring your lower back stays pressed against the pad throughout the movement. Avoid locking out knees at the top. (e.g., 150-250 lb for male, 80-150 lb for female).

exercises.name: Leg Extension
exercises.notes: Control the movement, squeezing the quads at the top. Avoid swinging the weight. (e.g., 60-90 lb for male, 30-50 lb for female).

exercises.name: Lying Hamstring Curl
exercises.notes: Focus on a strong contraction in the hamstrings, curling the weight towards your glutes. (e.g., 50-80 lb for male, 25-45 lb for female).

exercises.name: Glute Kickback Machine
exercises.notes: Focus on driving through the heel and squeezing the glute at the top of the movement. Maintain a stable core. (e.g., 30-50 lb for male, 15-30 lb for female).

exercises.name: Seated Calf Raise
exercises.notes: Go for a full stretch at the bottom and a strong squeeze at the top. (e.g., 80-120 lb for male, 40-70 lb for female).

exercises.name: Plank
exercises.notes: Maintain a straight line from head to heels, engaging your core and glutes. Avoid sagging your hips or arching your back.

exercises.name: Lat Pulldown (Wide Grip)
exercises.notes: Focus on pulling with your lats, driving your elbows down and back. Avoid leaning back excessively. (e.g., 80-120 lb for male, 40-70 lb for female).

exercises.name: Seated Cable Row (Neutral Grip)
exercises.notes: Keep your torso upright and pull the handle towards your lower abdomen, squeezing your shoulder blades together. (e.g., 70-110 lb for male, 35-65 lb for female).

exercises.name: Chest-Supported T-Bar Row
exercises.notes: This variation removes stress from the lower back. Focus on pulling with your upper back and squeezing. (e.g., 2-3 plates for male, 1-2 plates for female).

exercises.name: Machine Reverse Fly
exercises.notes: Engage your rear delts and upper back, pulling the handles apart. Keep the movement controlled. (e.g., 30-50 lb for male, 15-30 lb for female).

exercises.name: Dumbbell Bicep Curls
exercises.notes: Keep elbows tucked in and curl the dumbbells upwards, squeezing the bicep. Avoid swinging. (e.g., 17.5-25 lb per hand for male, 7.5-15 lb for female).

exercises.name: Hammer Curls
exercises.notes: Perform with a neutral grip (palms facing each other) to target the brachialis and brachioradialis. (e.g., 15-22.5 lb per hand for male, 7.5-12.5 lb for female).

exercises.name: Goblet Squat (Bodyweight or Light Dumbbell)
exercises.notes: Hold a light dumbbell or kettlebell against your chest. Focus on depth and keeping your chest up, distributing weight evenly through your feet. Prioritize form and only do if pain-free. (e.g., bodyweight to 20-30 lb dumbbell).

exercises.name: Single Arm Dumbbell Row (Supported)
exercises.notes: Support yourself on a bench with one hand and knee. Keep your back flat and pull the dumbbell towards your hip, squeezing your shoulder blade. (e.g., 20-35 lb for male, 10-20 lb for female).

exercises.name: Push-ups (on Knees or Elevated if needed)
exercises.reps: As many reps as possible (AMRAP) to failure
exercises.notes: Aim for controlled reps. If full push-ups are too challenging, use knee push-ups or place hands on an elevated surface.

exercises.name: Cable Face Pulls
exercises.notes: Use a rope attachment, pulling towards your face, externally rotating your shoulders. Excellent for upper back health and posture. (e.g., 30-50 lb for male, 15-30 lb for female).

exercises.name: Bird-Dog
exercises.notes: Slow and controlled movement. Keep your core tight and back stable, extending opposite arm and leg without rotating your hips.

exercises.name: Side Plank
exercises.notes: Maintain a straight line from head to heels. Engage your obliques and glutes.

exercises.name: Moderate Intensity Cardio (Elliptical, Bike, or Brisk Walk)
exercises.notes: Maintain a steady pace where you can talk but feel slightly out of breath. Focus on calorie expenditure and cardiovascular health without stressing the back.

exercises.name: Dynamic Stretching / Mobility Routine
exercises.notes: Perform light leg swings, arm circles, cat-cow, thoracic rotations, and other movements to improve flexibility and aid recovery. Listen to your body and avoid any movements that cause back pain.

exercises.name: Light Band Pull-Aparts
exercises.notes: Use a light resistance band, pulling it apart with straight arms. Focus on squeezing your shoulder blades together. Good for shoulder health and posture.

exercises.name: Glute Bridges
exercises.notes: Lie on your back, knees bent, feet flat. Lift your hips off the ground by squeezing your glutes. Avoid over-arching your lower back. Great for glute activation and lower back support.
